description:
Team CFSBR SpaceWeb is an interdisciplinary group driven by a passion for space exploration, open science, and technological innovation. We bring together diverse perspectives across analytics, software engineering, and scientific research to address complex aerospace challenges. By leveraging official NASA open datasets and modern web technologies, our goal is to build accessible, data-driven solutions that transform raw mission data into intuitive tools.

​Team Roster:

​Md Golam Mubasshir Rafi: Team Lead & Technical Architect

​Afshara Tasneem Zoa: Co-Lead & Research Lead

​Kaiba Hasnat: Frontend and UI Architecture

​Labiba Mahzabin: Planetary GIS and Data Engineering

​Nafiz Akib Khan: Power Systems and Feasibility Modeling

​Nishat Jahan Nowshin: Communications and Public Outreach

​What drives us?

Bridging the gap between complex space datasets and accessible software tools for researchers, students, and innovators, turning orbital challenges into grounded computational solutions.
summary:
SelenSync is an advanced lunar mission intelligence and landing-site decision-support platform developed by CFSBR SpaceWeb for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Addressing the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, it enables rapid comparison of lunar south pole landing sites and mission dates by visualizing Sun and Earth positions relative to the local horizon.

The platform integrates NASA LRO imagery, LOLA-derived terrain visualization, lunar ephemeris calculations, 360-degree horizon analysis, solar power and thermal simulations, Direct-to-Earth communications, and mission-specific feasibility assessments.

Its interactive 3D lunar globe, comparative telemetry dashboards, AI-powered mission assistant Asteria, and mission-plan exports create an accessible exploration environment.

A distinctive innovation is SelenSync's Mission Finance dashboard, which connects engineering constraints with battery requirements, mission-day costs, and capital risk. By combining planetary science, engineering, artificial intelligence, and techno-economic analysis, SelenSync supports more informed, resilient, and economically efficient lunar exploration planning.

Video Presentation (240 Seconds): https://youtu.be/VWCTo5uZ1Zc?si=3damtUnFeOlbfz-Q

What Does SelenSync Do and How Does It Work?

SelenSync is an advanced lunar mission intelligence and landing-site feasibility platform developed by CFSBR SpaceWeb. It integrates NASA planetary data, astronomical computation, geospatial intelligence, electrical engineering, telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and techno-economic analysis into a unified interactive mission control environment.

The lunar south pole presents extraordinary challenges for future exploration. Extremely low solar elevation, extensive crater shadows, severe thermal conditions, limited energy availability, and changing Earth visibility make landing-site selection a complex engineering problem.

A scientifically promising location may still be operationally unsuitable without sufficient sunlight, reliable communications, and sustainable power reserves.

SelenSync addresses these challenges by enabling users to explore lunar landing regions, compare mission dates, analyze Sun and Earth positions relative to local horizons, and investigate environmental, technical, and financial feasibility through an integrated web-based platform.

1. Core Technological Capabilities

Interactive 3D Lunar Exploration and Planetary GIS

SelenSync features an interactive three-dimensional lunar globe and geospatial exploration environment incorporating NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter imagery and LOLA-derived topographic visualization.

Users can explore lunar surface features, candidate landing regions, geological formations, historical mission locations, and geographic relationships across the lunar surface.

Advanced Solar and Earth Ephemeris

The platform computes time-dependent Sun and Earth positions using astronomical calculations and lunar rotational models.

Its computational engine incorporates solar elevation, azimuth, subsolar coordinates, lunar libration, and Earth visibility. NASA/JPL Horizons API integration provides an additional astronomical reference resource.

Users can investigate how changing mission dates and landing coordinates influence illumination conditions and communication opportunities.

360-Degree Horizon and Terrain Analysis

SelenSync incorporates a 360-degree analytical horizon profiling system to examine potential sunlight and Earth visibility obstruction caused by lunar crater rims, mountains, and surrounding highlands.

The platform distinguishes between geometric night, terrain obstruction, and unobstructed celestial visibility, helping users understand the environmental implications of different landing-site configurations.

Solar Power Generation and Battery Survival

The platform connects lunar illumination conditions with photovoltaic energy generation, spacecraft power requirements, and battery survival analysis.

Its engineering models incorporate solar array characteristics, conversion efficiency, grazing illumination, terrain shadowing, and battery storage capacity.

Users can investigate how shadow exposure affects power generation, energy reserves, and operational endurance.

Direct-to-Earth Communications and Deep Space Network Analysis

SelenSync evaluates lunar Earth visibility and communication feasibility through modeled RF link-budget calculations and Deep Space Network engineering references.

The platform represents NASA's three major DSN complexes at Goldstone, Madrid, and Canberra.

Its communication interfaces provide ground-station visibility assessments, RF indicators, communication status, and modeled handover information.

Thermal Survival and Cryogenic Risk Modeling

A Diviner-informed thermal analysis module examines lunar surface temperature scenarios, spacecraft heater requirements, cryogenic survival conditions, and battery depletion risks.

This connects lunar environmental conditions with spacecraft energy requirements and thermal survival considerations.

Multi-Site and Multi-Date Feasibility Comparison

SelenSync supports interactive comparison of candidate lunar landing sites and mission dates.

Users can investigate differences in solar elevation, electrical output, Earth visibility, communication feasibility, and operational conditions.

Interactive mission timelines and comparative telemetry enable users to explore the relationships between geographical location, mission timing, and landing-site suitability.

Commercial Lander and Mission-Specific Analysis

The platform incorporates configurable profiles representing commercial lunar landers and exploration vehicles.

These profiles support comparative analysis of solar arrays, battery systems, telecommunications, power requirements, and payload characteristics.

Interactive Mission Control and Telemetry

SelenSync integrates its scientific and engineering capabilities through a responsive aerospace-inspired mission control interface.

The platform provides telemetry dashboards, interactive scientific visualizations, mission timelines, landing-site comparisons, technical field guides, structured mission exports, and printable flight briefings.

2. Our Distinctive Innovation: Lunar Mission Finance

One of SelenSync's most significant innovations is its integration of aerospace engineering with techno-economic analysis.

Lunar mission feasibility is not exclusively a scientific or engineering problem. Decisions involving solar illumination, communication accessibility, thermal survival, and energy storage can influence spacecraft mass, payload capacity, operational expenditure, and capital allocation.

SelenSync introduces a dedicated Mission Finance and Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) Dashboard connecting these engineering constraints with financial decision-making.

Its analytical framework includes:

  • Battery Mass and Energy Storage Requirements
  • Potential Payload Delivery Cost Offsets
  • Levelized Cost of Mission Day (LCMD)
  • Capital-at-Risk Index (CaRI)
  • Operational and Financial Sensitivity Analysis
  • Comparative Landing-Site Economics
  • Mission Resource Allocation and Feasibility Assessment

Interactive scenario controls allow users to investigate how mission duration, shadow exposure, thermal power requirements, and scientific payload configurations influence projected financial and operational outcomes.

The dashboard incorporates capital allocation models, financial comparisons, risk indicators, and analytical visualizations.

This approach distinguishes SelenSync by connecting lunar mission engineering with economic efficiency, strategic resource allocation, and capital-risk assessment.

3. AI-Powered Lunar Mission Guidance

SelenSync incorporates Asteria, an interactive AI-powered lunar mission strategist designed to improve scientific accessibility and user engagement.

Asteria provides conversational assistance for exploring lunar science, mission architecture, solar illumination, communication constraints, and landing-site feasibility.

Its integration enables users to investigate complex scientific concepts through natural-language interaction while navigating the platform's technical features.

The AI guidance system complements SelenSync's astronomical, engineering, and financial computation modules.

4. Scientific Foundation and NASA Data Integration

SelenSync draws upon NASA and JPL scientific resources, planetary exploration research, and aerospace engineering literature.

Its scientific foundation includes:

NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO): Lunar surface imagery and planetary visualization.

Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA): Topographic reference data and elevation visualization for lunar terrain exploration.

NASA/JPL Horizons: Astronomical ephemeris resources supporting time-dependent celestial analysis.

NASA LRO Diviner: Lunar thermal research informing spacecraft temperature and survival models.

NASA Deep Space Network: Telecommunications engineering references supporting communication feasibility assessments.

NASA Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS): Commercial lunar mission information and spacecraft references supporting engineering scenarios.

The platform also incorporates scientific literature addressing polar illumination, lunar topography, thermal conditions, communication systems, and multi-criteria landing-site evaluation.

Together, these resources form the scientific foundation of SelenSync's integrated analytical and visualization environment.

5. Technology Stack and Development Architecture

SelenSync was developed as an interactive web application integrating scientific computing, geospatial visualization, and engineering analysis.

Frontend and Application Development

  • Next.js 16
  • React 19
  • TypeScript
  • Tailwind CSS
  • Radix UI Components

Astronomical and Engineering Computation

  • Astronomy Engine
  • Custom Lunar Ephemeris and Coordinate Transformations
  • Solar Power and Battery Modeling
  • RF Link-Budget Calculations
  • Thermal Survival Models
  • Techno-Economic Analysis Engine

Geospatial and 3D Visualization

  • Three.js
  • Leaflet
  • NASA Lunar Imagery and Topographic Layers
  • Custom SVG Horizon and Polar Visualizations
  • Interactive Geographic Interfaces

Analytical Visualization

  • Recharts
  • Comparative Telemetry Dashboards
  • Mission Finance Charts
  • Site Feasibility Matrices

AI Integration

  • Groq AI Services
  • Google Gemini Integration
  • Project-Specific Lunar Science Knowledge Base

Deployment and Collaboration

  • Vercel
  • GitHub
  • Next.js API Routes

The platform's architecture connects astronomical calculations, interactive visualization, mission scenario analysis, and techno-economic decision-support capabilities within one responsive environment.

6. What Makes SelenSync Creative and Distinctive?

SelenSync extends conventional lunar visualization by combining six interconnected dimensions of mission feasibility.

1. Terrain Intelligence: Understanding lunar geography, horizon obstruction, and landing-site characteristics.

2. Solar and Energy Intelligence: Connecting sunlight availability with power generation, energy storage, and battery survival.

3. Communication Intelligence: Investigating Earth visibility, RF link feasibility, and Deep Space Network connectivity.

4. Thermal and Operational Intelligence: Examining cryogenic survival, heater energy requirements, and environmental constraints.

5. Mission-Specific Feasibility: Comparing landing locations, mission dates, and commercial spacecraft configurations.

6. Techno-Economic Intelligence: Translating engineering constraints into financial scenarios, capital exposure indicators, and resource allocation decisions.

The integration of these dimensions creates a multidisciplinary decision-support environment for exploring complex lunar mission trade-offs.

Additional innovations include interactive 3D exploration, comparative mission timelines, AI-assisted scientific guidance, educational interfaces, and exportable mission intelligence.

7. What Benefits Does SelenSync Provide?

For Mission Planners and Engineers

SelenSync offers an integrated environment for preliminary landing-site comparison, engineering scenario exploration, and operational trade-off assessment.

For Planetary Researchers

The platform connects NASA resources, astronomical computation, geospatial visualization, and scientific indicators in an accessible research-oriented environment.

For Students and Educators

SelenSync makes lunar science, celestial geometry, power systems, and space communications easier to understand through interactive visualization and scientific explanations.

For Mission Economics and Strategic Planning

The Mission Finance dashboard demonstrates how physical engineering constraints can influence mission costs, payload decisions, operational efficiency, and capital risk.

For Multidisciplinary Space Innovation

SelenSync demonstrates how Finance, Computer Science, and Electrical and Electronic Engineering can contribute collaboratively to complex aerospace challenges.

8. Key Design and Development Considerations

Throughout development, our team emphasized several priorities.

Scientific Relevance: Aligning the platform with the environmental and operational challenges of lunar south pole exploration.

Integrated Analysis: Connecting terrain, illumination, communications, power systems, and mission economics.

User Experience: Presenting complex scientific information through intuitive navigation, interactive dashboards, and clearly organized telemetry.

Mission Flexibility: Supporting different locations, mission dates, and configurable spacecraft profiles.

Research Transparency: Providing publicly accessible source code, scientific references, analytical models, and project demonstrations.

Responsive Design: Developing interactive interfaces suitable for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.

Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Integrating scientific research, engineering development, financial modeling, and software architecture within a unified project.

9. Future Development and Research Potential

Our future development roadmap focuses on expanding SelenSync's scientific depth, technical capabilities, and research applications.

Planned enhancements include:

  • Higher-resolution lunar terrain integration
  • Expanded astronomical and topographic model validation
  • More detailed illumination and communication-window analysis
  • Advanced uncertainty and sensitivity modeling
  • Improved commercial lander parameter calibration
  • Expanded battery and thermal survival simulations
  • Advanced mission optimization and comparative scenario analysis
  • Enhanced educational and research-oriented exploration tools

Our long-term vision is to develop SelenSync into a comprehensive open research and educational platform for lunar mission feasibility and interdisciplinary space systems analysis.

10. Our Team: CFSBR SpaceWeb

CFSBR SpaceWeb is a six-member multidisciplinary team combining Finance, Computer Science, and Electrical and Electronic Engineering to develop SelenSync through collaborative research, software engineering, and scientific innovation.

Md Golam Mubasshir Rafi: Original Project Concept, Website Development, Product and System Architecture, Technical Integration, Mission Strategy, Techno-Economic Analysis, and Overall Project Coordination.

Afshara Tasneem Zoa: Scientific Research, Systems Strategy, Artemis Mission Case Architecture, and Research-Based Content Development.

Kaiba Hasnat: Avionics Interface, Aerospace Cockpit Design, and Telemetry Visualization.

Labiba Mahzabin: Planetary GIS, Lunar Topographic Data Engineering, and Spatial Visualization.

Nafiz Akib Khan: Electrical Power Systems, Solar Simulation, Battery Sizing, and Engineering Feasibility Modeling.

Nishat Jahan Nowshin: Mission Communications, Technical Documentation, Scientific Storytelling, and Public Engagement.

Project Demonstration and Original Narration: The 240-second technical presentation features original voice-over narration by Afshara Tasneem Zoa and Labiba Mahzabin, while the 30-second NASA global demonstration is narrated by Nishat Jahan Nowshin. All narration was recorded in the team members' own voices, with no AI-generated video footage or synthesized voices.

Collaborative Development: SelenSync reflects the team's combined contributions to original concept development, website engineering, scientific research, mission modeling, interactive visualization, documentation, and project presentation.

11. Conclusion: Connecting Lunar Science With Mission Intelligence

SelenSync is more than an interactive lunar map. It is an integrated mission intelligence and feasibility platform connecting planetary science, engineering, artificial intelligence, and mission economics.

By bringing NASA resources, celestial calculations, terrain analysis, communications assessments, energy modeling, and techno-economic decision support into one accessible environment, SelenSync demonstrates a multidisciplinary approach to future lunar exploration planning.

Developed by CFSBR SpaceWeb, the project reflects our commitment to scientific exploration, technological innovation, collaborative engineering, and research-driven problem-solving.

Our vision is to make lunar mission analysis more accessible, integrated, and actionable for the next generation of researchers, engineers, educators, and space innovators.
